title: Mike and distribution
statementMd:
Mike has always been thinking about the harshness of social inequality. He's so obsessed with it that sometimes it even affects him while solving problems. At the moment, Mike has two sequences of positive integers $*A* = [*a*_{1}, *a*_{2}, ..., *a*_{*n*}]$ and $*B* = [*b*_{1}, *b*_{2}, ..., *b*_{*n*}]$ of length $*n*$ each which he uses to ask people some quite peculiar questions.

To test you on how good are you at spotting inequality in life, he wants you to find an *"unfair"* subset of the original sequence. To be more precise, he wants you to select $*k*$ numbers $*P* = [*p*_{1}, *p*_{2}, ..., *p*_{*k*}]$ such that $1 ≤ *p*_{*i*} ≤ *n*$ for $1 ≤ *i* ≤ *k*$ and elements in $*P*$ are distinct. Sequence $*P*$ will represent indices of elements that you'll select from both sequences. He calls such a subset $*P*$ *"unfair"* if and only if the following conditions are satisfied: $2·(*a*_{*p*_{1}} + ... + *a*_{*p*_{*k*}})$ is **greater** than the sum of all elements from sequence $*A*$, and $2·(*b*_{*p*_{1}} + ... + *b*_{*p*_{*k*}})$ is **greater** than the sum of all elements from the sequence $*B*$. Also, $*k*$ should be smaller or equal to ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/e70d0af1413d58226605b883a776c3d3115f99a2.png) because it will be to easy to find sequence $*P*$ if he allowed you to select too many elements!

Mike guarantees you that a solution will always exist given the conditions described above, so please help him satisfy his curiosity!

## Input

The first line contains integer $*n*$ ($1 ≤ *n* ≤ 10^{5}$) — the number of elements in the sequences.

On the second line there are $*n*$ space-separated integers $*a*_{1}, ..., *a*_{*n*}$ ($1 ≤ *a*_{*i*} ≤ 10^{9}$) — elements of sequence $*A*$.

On the third line there are also $*n*$ space-separated integers $*b*_{1}, ..., *b*_{*n*}$ ($1 ≤ *b*_{*i*} ≤ 10^{9}$) — elements of sequence $*B*$.

## Output

On the first line output an integer $*k*$ which represents the size of the found subset. $*k*$ should be less or equal to ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/a469312c13fe74770be91238847356d82f74c170.png).

On the next line print $*k*$ integers $*p*_{1}, *p*_{2}, ..., *p*_{*k*}$ ($1 ≤ *p*_{*i*} ≤ *n*$) — the elements of sequence $*P*$. You can print the numbers in any order you want. Elements in sequence $*P*$ should be distinct.
statementZhMd:
Mike 一直在思考社会不平等的严酷性。他对这个问题如此着迷，以至于有时甚至会影响他解题。目前，Mike 有两个长度均为 $*n*$ 的正整数序列 $*A* = [*a*_{1}, *a*_{2}, ..., *a*_{*n*}]$ 和 $*B* = [*b*_{1}, *b*_{2}, ..., *b*_{*n*}]$，并用它们向人们提出一些相当奇怪的问题。

为了测试你在生活中发现不平等现象的能力，他希望你从原序列中找出一个“不公平”的子集。更准确地说，他希望你选出 $*k*$ 个数 $*P* = [*p*_{1}, *p*_{2}, ..., *p*_{*k*}]$，满足对于 $1 ≤ *p*_{*i*} ≤ *n*$（$1 ≤ *i* ≤ *k*$），并且 $*P*$ 中的元素互不相同。序列 $*P*$ 表示你将从两个序列中选取的元素的下标。当且仅当满足以下条件时，他称这样的子集 $*P*$ 是“不公平”的：$2·(*a*_{*p*_{1}} + ... + *a*_{*p*_{*k*}})$ **大于**序列 $*A*$ 中所有元素之和，并且 $2·(*b*_{*p*_{1}} + ... + *b*_{*p*_{*k*}})$ **大于**序列 $*B*$ 中所有元素之和。此外，$*k*$ 还应小于或等于 ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/e70d0af1413d58226605b883a776c3d3115f99a2.png)，因为如果允许你选择太多元素，就会很容易找到序列 $*P*$！

Mike 保证，在上述条件下始终存在解，所以请帮助他满足自己的好奇心！

## 输入格式

第一行包含一个整数 $*n*$（$1 ≤ *n* ≤ 10^{5}$），表示两个序列中的元素个数。

第二行包含 $*n*$ 个空格分隔的整数 $*a*_{1}, ..., *a*_{*n*}$（$1 ≤ *a*_{*i*} ≤ 10^{9}$），表示序列 $*A*$ 的元素。

第三行同样包含 $*n*$ 个空格分隔的整数 $*b*_{1}, ..., *b*_{*n*}$（$1 ≤ *b*_{*i*} ≤ 10^{9}$），表示序列 $*B*$ 的元素。

## 输出格式

第一行输出一个整数 $*k*$，表示找到的子集的大小。$*k*$ 应小于或等于 ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/a469312c13fe74770be91238847356d82f74c170.png)。

下一行输出 $*k*$ 个整数 $*p*_{1}, *p*_{2}, ..., *p*_{*k*}$（$1 ≤ *p*_{*i*} ≤ *n*$），表示序列 $*P*$ 中的元素。你可以按任意顺序输出这些数。序列 $*P*$ 中的元素应当互不相同。
